name: Find and publish jobs
description: Search your chosen sources for roles that fit your goals.
whenToUse: Running or resuming an authorized job search.
instructions:
## Personal context for Discover fit analysis
Before assessing a role, read the current selected profile through read_search_context and read_personal_context for current candidate evidence. The profile instructions section named 'What your agent knows' contains exactly four optional labeled notes mapping to matchAssessment: Skills & experience -> skillsExperience; Compensation -> compensation; Wellbeing & culture -> wellbeingCulture; Location & work setting -> locationWorkSetting. Use these notes together with the selected resume, verified background and explicit preferences; empty notes are missing context, never neutral or negative evidence.
During authorized profile setup or updates, when saving relevant context learned in conversation, read the current profile and preserve all filters, priorities, prose and other fields; update only the appropriate labeled notes through save_search_profile with current expectedVersion, then read back. Write each section as a short, current decision brief: what matters to the user, what makes a role a good fit, and any important tradeoff or unknown. Include only information that could change a role evaluation. Synthesize rather than append, and never turn an assumption into a preference. Existing Career goals & tradeoffs and Profile evaluation notes remain applicable legacy evidence; preserve them and reconcile conflicts with the user rather than silently recategorizing or deleting them.
For each of the four scores, compare specific employer evidence with the matching personal context: explain what matches, the material tension or gap, and what still needs verification. Skills & experience must distinguish demonstrated ability, desired growth and unsupported requirements. Compensation must compare disclosed pay/benefits with actual needs; missing pay or an unknown personal threshold limits conclusions. Wellbeing & culture needs evidence about hours, management, support and working practices, never brand-based assumptions. Location & work setting must check geographic remote eligibility, commute/travel and relocation conditions, without inferring consent.
When the user requests a saved personal report, publish this analysis in recommendation.matchAssessment with all four score/reasoning entries, an assessedAt timestamp, and recommendation.evaluatedProfileVersion set to the profile version actually used. Each reasoning is at most 240 characters and should name a concrete personal criterion and role fact or missing fact. Use null for scores without enough evidence; never invent a score to complete the display. Write recommendation.whyItFits and materialGap using the connected narrative contract below. A must-have conflict stays explicit and cannot be averaged away. Profile edits make previous assessments stale; reassess on the next authorized evaluation and publish a new batch rather than rewriting historical analysis. Context never grants application, sharing or messaging permission.

## Per-job narrative in Discover
Default to a compact, team-focused decision brief, about 130–180 words per role; expand only when the user requests deeper analysis. Lead with the existing recommendation.priority plus one short verdict. Use up to five short labeled bullets in chat: Team, Your contribution, Your growth, Support, Practical fit. Close with one sentence saying what would raise or lower the priority. Do not append a research diary, a changes-made section or a separate match-strength tag.
Team: Explain what the actual team owns, its users/product and relevant technical problems. Establish the exact squad/manager where possible; otherwise say placement is unknown. Research the exact posting/team first. Use related-team postings and company material only as clearly labeled adjacent context, never as proof of this team's stack, culture, mentorship or your assignment. Link the few sources supporting material claims; distinguish direct evidence, adjacent context, inference and unknowns in ordinary wording without labeling every sentence.
Your contribution: Connect specific demonstrated candidate work to what this team needs, explaining the contribution rather than listing matching keywords. Never infer an unlisted stack or responsibility.
Your growth: Distinguish what you already offer from what this team could teach you. Connect ownership to your goals and distinguish product breadth from backend/systems depth. Discuss service design, data models, production reliability or other relevant responsibilities only when supported; identify the consequential ownership question when unknown.
Support: Assess concrete evidence for mentoring, onboarding, design/code review and production/on-call support. A promise to work with senior engineers is not proof of structured mentorship. Team-specific evidence outweighs general employer claims; unknown working practices remain unknown.
Practical fit: Summarize only decision-relevant pay with its original period, location/work arrangement, start date and eligibility/clearance conditions. Do not repeat every job fact or turn unknowns into negatives. Read the exact eligibility wording, including whether internships count toward an experience limit. Existing user-requested clearance visibility and conditional graduation rules still apply.
For saved Discover analysis, reuse recommendation.whyItFits for the Team, Your contribution and Your growth substance; use recommendation.materialGap for consequential Support/Practical fit uncertainties and the conditional priority sentence. Keep these existing plain-text fields concise and readable in the current renderer; do not require Markdown rendering or add new fields. Omit materialGap when no material concern is supported. Save the existing priority separately, keeping both fields consistent with the four matchAssessment dimensions, current profile version and actual evidence. The four short score reasons supplement this synthesis; do not repeat each one or manufacture concerns to fill categories.
Illustrative structure only; never copy unsupported facts:
Strong Consider — relevant product experience; backend scope and timing need confirmation.
- Team: The posting describes consumer features and APIs; your exact squad is not established.
- Your contribution: Your interface and backend work gives you a starting point for full-stack delivery.
- Your growth: End-to-end ownership could develop judgment; verify whether it includes services and data models.
- Support: Senior collaboration is advertised; structured mentoring and on-call support are unknown.
- Practical fit: State the actual disclosed pay/period, work setting and timing or eligibility question.
Priority rises if timing works and the assigned squad offers backend ownership with concrete mentorship.
Write directly to the user as "you". Never invent a match to justify a search result; clearly unrelated work returns to selection review, while weaker relevant matches stay visible with tradeoffs. Priority directs order and tailoring effort, not blanket exclusion or application permission.

Before submitting any search_ats job, call read_search_context(profileId) and read_search_filter_plan(profileId). The latter runs the original pinned Career Ops validator and offline provider/query audit, reports exact effective config, versions and missing targeting, and performs no search. If saved Roles exist without title keywords, the backend now refuses collection rather than treating every title as relevant. Load career-adjacent-titles and its reference when deriving role-family keywords from the selected resume, target roles and deal-breakers. Carry out already authorized targeting setup yourself; do not silently expand the user's career goals, retire intentionally chosen targets, change Required/Preferred/Flexible strengths or apply upstream example criteria. Ask only for a meaningful unresolved choice. Never replace semantic role-family selection with splitting literal UI labels into a narrow exact-title whitelist.

Save per-profile scanner controls through save_search_document(kind=profile,id=profileId,expectedVersion=currentVersion), preserving frontmatter and all existing narrative, and add or update one section named "## Career Ops discovery filters" containing exactly one fenced json object. Example: {"title_filter":{"positive":["Backend","Software Engineer"],"negative":["word:Senior"]},"skip_tiers":["senior"]}. Read back the profile and read_search_filter_plan before enqueueing. These are examples of shape, never default user targets. The section supports original title_filter, skip_tiers, location_filter, max_posting_age_days, posted_after, posted_before, content_filter, country_eligibility_filter, visa_filter, salary_filter and re_apply_windows. Keys replace the same shared fallback key for this profile only. Do not edit shared portal targeting to retarget one profile, discard other profile text or sources, invent salary/country/cooldown facts, or configure controls the plan rejects. An explicitly saved empty title_filter is a deliberate broad search and must be described as such. Profile location defaults remain Preferred; location_filter is an explicit hard scanner gate, not a geographic radius. Country-limited remote work still needs eligibility review. skip_tiers reuses classify-tier.mjs: plain/unrecognized titles default to mid, so excluding mid would discard ordinary unlevelled roles. Never equate a title tier with actual years-of-experience eligibility.

The original Career Ops fetchJdViaKnownApi now supplies full-description retrieval for Lever, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters and embedded Greenhouse as well as ordinary Greenhouse. Liveness, full text and employer metadata remain separate requirements; metadata-incomplete or inaccessible postings remain diagnostics, never invented saved jobs. Some provider descriptions can therefore now be saved, but bounded source coverage, API limits and manual browser/web research remain necessary. Do not claim every source is covered.

Before publishing, treat shortlist.retainedListingIds as a queue for personal fit analysis, not a competition for a small number of slots. Surface most verified relevant and plausibly eligible roles. Ask “How good a fit is this job?” and use the answer for priority and depth of tailoring, not whether the agent works on it at all. Hide only clearly unrelated roles, expired/duplicate postings, or confirmed mandatory eligibility conflicts under the user's actual or explicitly authorized conditional search scenarios. Missing clearance, citizenship, team details, salary, preferred experience or start-date confirmation is unknown, not a negative fact. Preserve plausible opportunities with a concrete requirement or gap. If the user wants clearance roles visible, keep them visible and distinguish active clearance required at application/start from clearance obtainable after hire; never assume the user does or does not hold it. Do not hide real software engineering work just because the company is non-tech, the team is corporate, the pay is modest, the rotations are broad, or the match is not exceptional. Explicit current named-employer exclusions still apply unless the user changes them. Record actual skips with evidence when a supported canonical record exists.

Within an already authorized request, handle routine tool selection, profile selection/setup, scoped writes and bounded error recovery yourself when your runtime policy permits. Inspect current tools, schemas and owned state before concluding a capability is missing or asking for developer help. Reuse an equivalent search profile; when the requested targeting clearly differs, use save_search_profile with a new id and expectedVersion 0 (or save_search_document for a new profile document) to create an owned search profile, preserving existing profiles and unrelated preferences. A new search profile is targeting, not fabricated candidate facts or broader permission. Ask only about meaningful preferences, missing facts, necessary consent or a runtime approval requirement. Never change permissions, human verification, submission approvals, sharing or schedules to work around a blocker.

For an independently requested search, read_search_context, choose or create the matching profile, and use request_search_sweep when handing work to the personal-agent inbox; queued means waiting for an agent to claim and execute, not search completed. create_agent_task is the onboarding-step-specific path: inspect read_onboarding_state and its preconditions rather than calling it blindly during connection_pending or advancing onboarding just to bypass a guard. For immediate authorized execution, use the existing search guide and available tools, then publish and read back the private batch so Discover receives actual results. Do not stop at saving observations or a shortlist. After an uncertain write, inspect current state before retrying with the same event key; do not duplicate tasks, forge receipts, or invent missing infrastructure. Respect explicit stop/report-only requests, safety and runtime approval boundaries. When valid authorized alternatives are unavailable, report the practical blocker instead of running work off-book.

For a daily job scan, use the selected profile and configured discovery sources; never restrict the daily scan to a single proof employer unless the user asks. SimplifyJobs Summer2027-Internships and New-Grad-Positions are default lead sources, not availability or eligibility evidence. Read paginated aggregate leads with read_search_source_leads for the configured owned source; follow nextOffset rather than silently discarding remaining leads. Use supported copied Career Ops providers for employer verification. For the normal configured scan use one backend search_ats job and consume its saved shortlist. For additional web research or unsupported sources, your runtime can perform searches and submit 1–25 resulting canonical employer URLs through submit_search_leads, then explicitly rescreen that supplemental research against current settings. Read current schemas and the application-workspace guide. Screening is deterministic triage with met/unmet/unknown checks, not personal narrative analysis or submission authorization. You generate the role-specific analysis and four score/reasoning dimensions from actual candidate evidence, then publish_batch and prepare_draft. Verify every saved result with owned reads and confirm the website renders the same records. Missing search capability, blocked provider, truncated coverage, missing applicant context, ambiguous preferences, context conflicts and publication mismatches must remain explicit; never turn them into completed daily scans.

screen_search_discoveries is discovery-gate triage with contractVersion 1, evaluationScope discovery-gates and applicantEligibility not-evaluated. Its typed employment/work-setting constraints reject unsupported values, preserve multiple selected arrangements and distinguish Required/Preferred/Flexible. A not-applicable check means no configured gate; unknown means evidence is missing. Retained/review-needed is not a positive applicant match. The operation does not evaluate experience, graduation, availability, authorization, prior applications or company limits; reconcile those separately with current evidence. Do not claim that passing the filter is a complete résumé-based eligibility check.

The backend verification stage checks every submitted link with copied Career Ops ATS APIs and guarded sequential browser fallback when inconclusive. Per-link diagnostics distinguish status active/expired/uncertain (with code, reason, checkedAt, method) from extraction parsed/unsupported/failed/not-attempted. An active link with unsupported or failed parsing is still active, but is not a complete saved job ready for analysis. Never call a bot wall, timeout, missing browser or browser_budget_exhausted a closed posting. The bounded browser budget can leave explicit uncertainty; inspect diagnostics in owned run source checkpoints or intake results and report coverage honestly. No new schedule, report, publication or application is authorized by liveness checks.

Lookout is a portable career context harness; the connected personal agent supplies all reasoning, browsing and execution. Before discovery load career-find-jobs and read_search_context. Canonical profile documents own per-profile rules and targeting; portals documents retain source configuration; candidate facts, company lists, resumes and applications remain existing owned records. Save context changes through save_search_document or existing versioned preference tools. Start/resume durable search runs, checkpoint sources, save discoveries and screening evidence, then publish selected jobs through publish_batch. Bounded Node jobs can execute supported configured source scans using the copied Career Ops layer; the agent runtime supplies web searches, unsupported source research and personal analysis. Stored observations are evidence, not verified personal eligibility. No local runner, Career Ops checkout or fixed agent vendor is required for this workflow. Never activate schedules from defaults. A new account with missing context needs one focused intent question and an initial profile/portal configuration, not a template author’s facts. Search tasks carry searchProfileId/mode; claim before work and use them to start/resume the run. Check current evidence and prior applications before publishing. Report blocked/truncated sources and finish partial when coverage is incomplete.

Record skipped canonical roles with record_selection_decision, supporting posting evidence and the relevant preference. Explicit current policy exclusions are firm; discretionary fit judgments remain uncertain. Read skipped opportunities on request and at the next scan to honor reconsideration requests; preferences and fresh live verification still apply. Keep skipped roles out of default digests. Occasionally mention a useful recurring preference pattern through authorized text delivery, respecting quiet mode; do not send a list on every run.

Publish dynamic job research in private recommendation: whyItFits, materialGap, optional matchAssessment {assessedAt:ISO timestamp,skillsExperience:{score,reasoning},compensation:{score,reasoning},wellbeingCulture:{score,reasoning},locationWorkSetting:{score,reasoning}}, optional sourceFreshness and searchProfileId. Scores need current job/profile evidence; omit them when unavailable. Generate all four dimension records yourself. Each score is 0–100 or null when unknown, with one short evidence-based reasoning sentence up to 240 characters. Optional overall percent is agent-generated, never inferred by the UI; optional evidence is limited to 1000 characters. Store this JSON on the existing private batch recommendation; no separate assessment table or scoring engine exists. Cards show four numbers (Unknown for null); Preview reveals reasoning. Legacy factor assessments remain readable. Discovery workers do not generate scores. Use the Per-job narrative in Discover contract for whyItFits and materialGap; do not require an invented concern. Source freshness describes actual observation recency, with an explicit date and a label for results older than 72 hours; postedDate stays null when undisclosed. Never put personal assessment in public employer facts. UI rarity derives from owned company tier placements and the selected profile list, never agent-supplied rarity or fixed company names. Unranked roles remain visible. Use prepare_draft to save exact employer questions and proposed answers, binding completed reusable answers to profileField or savedAnswerId/savedAnswerVersion and attached files to fieldType=file. Do not invent generic contact requirements. Missing answers and custom answers awaiting review appear in the UI; agents cannot grant human review, reuse consent or submission approval. Existing historical batches remain immutable; publish a new batch/eventKey for new research.

## Direct search with temporary staging
The shared hosted-board collection/publishing path remains disabled. Private Discover publication is the final step of an authorized job search, after agent personal fit analysis; never publish the raw or merely filter-passed shortlist. Do not ask for a second confirmation to complete that already requested search output. No local runner is required in the personal agent runtime: the configured Node API and worker own execution. Read the selected profile and read_search_filter_plan, resolve missing targeting, then call submit_backend_job once with kind search_ats and the profileId. Poll read_backend_jobs; a queue acknowledgement is not a completed search.
Pipeline version 2 collects concurrently into private run-scoped temporary files on the worker's persistent Docker volume. Metadata title/seniority filters run before verification; full filters run before shortlist persistence. Rejected postings are not saved as permanent discoveries. Expired leases cannot write; interrupted work resumes committed staging checkpoints.
Only a completed or partial job with pipelineVersion 2 and result.shortlist is ready for agent analysis. shortlist.totalRetained is the full count. retainedListingIds is a preview of at most 100 IDs, not a selection cap. Read every page of read_search_discoveries with runId and limit 100, advancing nextOffset until null; do not stop at the preview. Report coverage honestly. Unchanged previously saved jobs and tracked applications are excluded; materially changed jobs may return for review.
Read candidate context and assess the saved shortlist using the four personal dimensions above. A passed discovery filter does not establish personal eligibility. Preserve unknown graduation, authorization, availability and team facts as review-needed. After personal fit analysis, publish the relevant, live, non-duplicate opportunities that remain plausibly eligible through publish_batch so they appear in private Discover. Never publish a shared/hosted board automatically. Applications, statuses, approvals and submission evidence remain untouched by search. Each recommendation must include searchListingId, searchRunId, searchProfileId, evaluatedProfileVersion, whyItFits, any materialGap, and all four matchAssessment score/reasoning dimensions, with null scores for missing evidence. Employer facts and descriptions must come from the exact verified posting; keep personal analysis in private recommendation. Confirmed mandatory conflicts stay out unless the user explicitly requests conditional visibility, such as clearance roles or an alternate graduation scenario. Unknown eligibility and weaker fit stay visible with clear flags; do not turn a preference into an exclusion. If none are relevant, report that outcome rather than add unrelated work.
Source freshness is based on verified employer evidence; source age alone is not an exact employer posting date. Preferred constraints are not hard exclusions unless configured as required. All configured sources are attempted; blocked or incomplete providers keep the result partial.
## Complete the private Discover handoff
Treat result.shortlist.reporting=pending-muse as unfinished personal review, not a failed scan or permission to publish raw results. Read the finished job, all shortlist pages, current search profile, candidate evidence, existing application links and current owned batch. Refresh expired or uncertain employer evidence using supported verification before recommending. The selected profile owns required exclusions and availability; do not infer personal eligibility from the discovery screening or employer country. Do not require another user request after completing analysis in an already authorized search.
After analysis, call publish_batch in chunks of at most 100 selected jobs, using stable keys based on the source run, evaluated profile version and chunk number, for example discover:<runId>:profile:<version>:part:<index>. Preserve the exact payload while reconciling an uncertain publication; read the returned batch before retrying. Redelivered backend-job events must reuse the same source run and publication keys, never start another search or create duplicate batches. Include the original run/listing IDs in every private recommendation so Discover links to its archived evidence. Store no fabricated fit scores or candidate facts in public employer records.
Read back every returned batch with read_batch(batchId), verify each selected canonical URL, source IDs and saved four-dimension assessment, and confirm those items use the website's private batch projection before saying Discover is populated. A publish acknowledgement alone is insufficient. The backend worker receipt remains an immutable scan receipt; do not rewrite it to invent agent completion. A completed scan is not a published Discover batch. Empty/ineligible results, partial source coverage, publication errors and missing agent execution remain explicit.
The connected personal agent executes this handoff when it handles the authorized completion event; these guides do not install or activate a background model or wake delivery. Never claim unattended analysis is running without an actual host receipt.
## Supplemental manual research
Agent browsing can research blocked sources on an authorized request. The legacy save_search_discoveries and screening tools remain available for explicit manual workflows; do not use them to persist an unfiltered source dump or duplicate the normal backend job.
## Resume a finished backend job
Read the existing job and its kind before acting. Do not enqueue another search because a completion event was redelivered. For search_ats read the full saved shortlist and current profile, complete personal fit analysis, then perform the private Discover handoff above. Application jobs use application-workspace. Preserve application status and human approval. No automatic messages, schedules, applications or hosted-board publication.

This is a Lookout adaptation of the pinned Career Ops workflow. Never fabricate candidate facts, posting evidence, eligibility, or submission receipts. Load cold-outreach for context-aware suggestions during relevant authorized work; sending still requires explicit permission.


## Match strength, preparation volume and compensation
Reuse recommendation.priority (Apply Now, Strong Consider, Skip Unless Team Fit) to express relative match and application priority, alongside the existing four matchAssessment dimensions and evidence-based whyItFits/materialGap. Apply Now identifies the strongest actionable matches; Strong Consider covers plausible relevant opportunities; Skip Unless Team Fit marks lower-priority or team-dependent opportunities and is not an instruction to hide a role or stop otherwise authorized preparation. Do not add a separate narrative strength label, overall score or percentile. There is no separate displayed matchStrength field; do not claim one was saved or add a new database schema for this instruction update. Priority never grants submission permission.
Close fit determines priority and tailoring effort, not whether Muse performs already authorized application preparation for other relevant eligible roles. During an authorized application-work request, prepare accurate baseline answers for routine plausible matches using current permitted evidence; reserve deeper company/team research, customized narratives and resume tailoring for stronger matches. Unknown facts block only affected answers or submission, not all independent preparation. Never fabricate answers, consent, clearance or graduation changes to increase volume. Search-only requests do not authorize application preparation or submission; keep approval, authorization and uncertain-outcome safeguards intact.
Use current, dated new-graduate salary benchmarks with the closest available degree, role and geography. Separate base salary from bonus/equity/total compensation and actual salaries from projections. A disclosed salary is known even when compensation fit is uncertain. Compare the posted range to the benchmark and give a qualified fit assessment; an exact percentile needs distribution data. Missing pay is an explicit unknown, not an exclusion. Compensation affects ranking, not a hard cutoff unless the user explicitly sets one.
Honor conditional search scenarios without overwriting candidate facts: a December graduation internship scenario is not a confirmed education change or permission to answer an employer form with that date. State which scenario makes the role plausible and what must actually change. Broad industry and team preferences should guide the explanation, not silently exclude relevant engineering roles.


Employer-disclosed pay belongs in recommendation.jobFacts.compensation when publishing an existing job, alongside sourceUrl, checkedAt, workSetting and sponsorship. Preserve the currency, original amount/range and pay period verbatim (hour/week/month/year), including base versus bonus/equity distinctions. Never annualize monthly internship pay or copy a comparison benchmark into this employer fact. Use explicit Not disclosed when the employer does not disclose pay; omit the observation only when no refreshed pay evidence was checked. Cards read this observed compensation before the catalog value and do not extract pay from personal fit prose. This does not change fit ratings, shared catalog facts or application consent.


## Broad lead coverage and unresolved-link recovery
Treat collection and shortlist selection as separate stages. For enabled Jobright new-grad and internship lists, retain every published row in the existing temporary volume before title triage or employer-link resolution, including filtered titles and unresolved links. The public lists advertise a seven-day subset, not exhaustive market coverage. Retained pools expire after seven days; they are not Discover cards, employer-verified facts or permanent database discoveries.
After a direct search, inspect result.retainedLeads, pendingLeadResolution and sourceAccounting. Page read_search_source_leads(runId,sourceId,offset,limit) through nextOffset for every relevant retained Jobright source. It returns owned raw rows, source-listed date/work setting, resolution and triage status, including title-excluded leads. Never claim full verification merely because the worker finished. A missing or expired pool requires a new authorized search; do not reconstruct historical counts from today's feed.
For plausible unresolved leads, research the employer careers site using exact company, role title and location. Match the actual posting and public canonical application URL; never guess URLs or use a different team/role as evidence. Pass resolved URLs through the existing submit_search_leads verifier in bounded batches, screen with the current profile and deduplicate against current jobs/application history before private publication. If no exact posting can be established, retain/report the lead as unresolved rather than silently treating it as rejected or verified. No worker LLM, new database lead store or application automation is implied.
Recognize common engineering title aliases for an explicitly selected role family; negative seniority and unrelated-role rules still apply. For US-wide profile targeting, explicit country/state evidence can match, an explicit foreign country can exclude, and incomplete city/country evidence stays unknown pending employer verification. Preserve explicit scanner location restrictions and narrower city targets. Freshness comes from the current saved profile: this user's authorized window is seven days. Missing employer dates stay unknown; a feed's displayed date is source recency, never an invented employer posting date.
Report source totals, title exclusions, unresolved links, verified/filtered candidates and final shortlist counts separately. Counts of raw leads are not counts of unique eligible jobs; final shortlist deduplication and all application safeguards remain required.


## Recall before ranking
For a selected software-engineering family, include MTS/Member of Technical Staff, junior/associate developer, application development, platform and GPU/graphics engineering variants for review. MTS is a role family, not proof of the senior Staff rank. Do not infer seniority from Staff inside Member of Technical Staff, or treat an unexplained company level as a confirmed senior requirement. A bracketed multi-level range explicitly including Junior/Entry/Associate is review-needed rather than senior-only. Explicit Senior/Principal/Staff rank outside those contexts and the user's explicit role exclusions still apply. Preserve literal posting titles, including brackets, for identity and display.
Unknown start date, team, experience level, citizenship/clearance status and personal fit stay questions to verify, not invented negatives. Keep confirmed constraints visible and distinguish them from preferences: a confirmed incompatible required date or eligibility condition must be explained, while an undisclosed condition is unknown. Never assume the candidate lacks citizenship or clearance; preserve the user's instruction to surface clearance roles with the exact requirement flagged. Employer-confirmed closure is an actual exclusion from live recommendations even if a lead list still contains the role.
Give the user a broad Worth a look group alongside Top picks in chat/digests using existing recommendation.priority and four fit dimensions; do not add a separate match tag, database field or approval state. Apply Now identifies the best researched actionable opportunities; Strong Consider includes other verified relevant plausible opportunities with concise preliminary analysis and explicit unknowns. Missing team detail or a low/unknown fit score does not justify withholding a relevant role. Keep minimum agent analysis before Discover publication; reserve deeper team research and tailoring for the best opportunities. Do not invent a score, team fact or positive claim to fill the broad group. Existing plain-text fields remain the source of the saved rationale.
For retained Jobright pools, first page read_search_source_leads with resolution=unresolved to focus recovery work; sourceTotal remains the complete pool count while total/nextOffset cover the unresolved selection. companyWebsite and researchQuery are lead hints only. Check the exact employer posting for title/location/requisition identity and liveness; use current owned history to reuse known canonical URLs when the match is established, avoiding repeated research without assuming that similar titles are identical. Unsupported or ambiguous matches stay unresolved and visible in coverage accounting. Report how many links were recovered, expired, ambiguous or still pending, and never call the search complete merely because broader filtering produced a larger unresolved pool. The worker does not operate a search engine: employer research belongs to the connected agent, followed by supported verification, full filtering, deduplication and scoped publication.


## Single-portal search and focused demos
For a user-requested employer/portal search, read_search_context and choose the exact enabled tracked_companies ID. Call submit_portal_search with kind=search_ats, input={profileId,portalId}, and a stable eventKey. This queues the existing direct pipeline for exactly that portal; do not disable other saved portals, change profile filters or submit an all-source job as a substitute. For two portals, use separate stable requests and finish/reconcile each run before starting the next for that profile. Report supported collection and verification separately; an unsupported TikTok/ByteDance parser or blocked endpoint is a coverage limitation, not zero jobs.
A request for the top two roles limits the final agent recommendation, not source collection or verification. After completion, page the entire shortlist, deduplicate overlapping roles across portal runs and current application history, apply current candidate/team fit analysis, and select up to two strongest verified relevant matches. If fewer than two can be established, say so; do not manufacture scores or replace missing evidence with collection metadata. Preserve the existing publication and application safeguards.


## Typed Discover publication
Use the current publish_batch inputSchema as the card JSON contract. For each new canonicalUrl provide employer.company and title (nonempty strings, up to 200 characters), employmentType (exactly FT or Internship), and location (string up to 1000 characters; empty if unknown). Full-time is a display label, not an enum value. Verify employment type rather than defaulting an unknown role to FT. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD or null when undisclosed; locations is an array of strings. Other public employer fields use their schema types and bounds. Keep private priority, fit analysis, gaps and profile evidence under recommendation. Existing catalog jobs may use jobId; do not invent missing facts. Known full-time label aliases are normalized by the backend for compatibility, but always send the canonical enum. Read back the published batch and verify employer.employmentType before claiming the Discover cards are ready. A validation error is an unsaved batch; correct the named field and retry only under the existing event-key rules.
expectedOutput: A saved filtered verified shortlist followed by agent personal fit analysis
Relevant plausible jobs published after personal fit analysis, with match strength, requirements and tradeoffs
Honest source coverage, unknown eligibility and new/changed counts; no shared hosted-board publication

context: search profile and its independent rules
